blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Global trade, viewed from the executive floor, is no longer a sequence of transactions — it is an architecture. Flows of capital, goods, information and risk move through a lattice of ports, banks, regulators, carriers, courts and counterparties, each of which can be a strength or a fault line, depending on the week.

What distinguishes a strategic view from an operational one is the willingness to step back and ask why the architecture is the way it is, and what pressures are likely to reshape it. Concentrated ports, thin shipping lanes, dominant clearing currencies, fragile trade corridors: these are not weather events. They are choices, made decades ago, that the current generation of leaders must either defend, reinforce, or quietly replace.

The companies that thrive across cycles tend to hold two pictures of the trade architecture in mind at once: the version that exists today, which feeds the quarter, and the version that may exist in ten years, which decides whether the business is still interesting at all. Both pictures deserve deliberate attention.

items.q: How does the text redefine global trade for the executive audience?
options: As a set of weather events
items.why: "is no longer a sequence of transactions — it is an architecture."

items.q: According to the text, what distinguishes a strategic view from an operational one?
options: The willingness to step back and ask why the architecture is as it is
The size of the shipping fleet
A focus on this quarter's numbers
items.why: "the willingness to step back and ask why the architecture is the way it is."

items.q: The author calls concentrated ports and thin shipping lanes "not weather events" in order to suggest that…
options: they are unpredictable and beyond anyone's control
they are deliberate choices that can be changed
they matter only to logistics teams
items.why: Inferência: opor a "weather events" enfatiza que são escolhas humanas — "They are choices, made decades ago."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The current architecture is simply the natural, unavoidable order of things.
Leaders should weigh both the present and a ten-year view.
Today's trade fault lines were shaped by past decisions.
A lattice of relationships underpins trade flows.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que a arquitetura é fruto de escolhas — logo, discordaria de que ela é 'natural e inevitável'.

items.q: What does holding "two pictures" of the architecture at once imply about strong companies?
options: They ignore the current quarter to focus on the future
They rely on a single dominant currency
They balance near-term performance with long-term relevance
They change their strategy every quarter
items.why: Inferência: uma imagem 'alimenta o trimestre' e a outra decide 'se o negócio ainda é interessante' — presente e futuro juntos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James abrir a discussão do conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. Before we get into numbers, I want to frame today differently. We usually review trade as a set of lanes and contracts. This morning I'd like us to look at it as an architecture — and to ask which parts of it could look very different in ten years.

Start with concentration. A striking share of our volume clears through three ports and settles in one currency. On a calm day, that's efficiency. On a bad day, it's a single fault line running under the whole business. None of it was decided by us; it was inherited, and we've quietly reinforced it every year since.

My worry is not this quarter. This quarter is fine. My worry is that the corridors we depend on are being reshaped by decisions taken in capitals, not in boardrooms. So I'm asking each of you to bring one scenario to the next session: name a corridor you think is fragile, and tell me what we'd do the week it closes.

If we can hold today's map and a plausible future map in mind at the same time, we'll make far better calls than if we simply defend what we have.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does James want the board to look at trade this morning?
options: As a set of lanes and contracts
As a legal question for the courts
items.why: "I'd like us to look at it as an architecture."

items.q: What does James say about the company's concentration in three ports and one currency?
options: It was carefully chosen by the current board
It was inherited and quietly reinforced every year
It affects only the finance team
items.why: "it was inherited, and we've quietly reinforced it every year since."

items.q: What does James ask each board member to bring to the next session?
options: A scenario naming a fragile corridor and a response if it closes
A list of new ports to acquire
A summary of this quarter's results
items.why: "name a corridor you think is fragile, and tell me what we'd do the week it closes."

items.q: When James says concentration is "efficiency on a calm day" but "a single fault line on a bad day," he is suggesting that…
options: the same design can be a strength or a serious risk depending on conditions
the company should always maximise efficiency
bad days are extremely rare and can be ignored
items.why: Inferência: a mesma concentração vira vantagem ou vulnerabilidade conforme o cenário — o ponto é o duplo gume.

items.q: What is implied by "reshaped by decisions taken in capitals, not in boardrooms"?
options: The company should relocate its head office
The board makes all the important trade decisions
Capital cities have better logistics than boardrooms
The main threats are geopolitical and outside the company's direct control
items.why: Inferência: 'capitais' = governos/geopolítica; o risco vem de fora, não das decisões internas da empresa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Trade flows through a lattice of ports, banks and carriers." A lattice is…
options: an interlocking network of connected elements
items.why: Lattice = malha / entrelaçamento — uma rede de elementos interligados.

items.q: "A firm's dependence on one route is a hidden fault line." A fault line here means…
options: a point of structural weakness that could break under stress
items.why: Fault line = linha de falha: ponto de fragilidade estrutural que pode ceder sob pressão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When the Red Sea route closed, the whole ___ was rerouted for months."
items.why: Trade corridor = corredor comercial, a rota por onde o comércio flui.

items.q: A clearing currency is best described as…
options: the currency in which cross-border payments are settled
the local currency of a single port
a currency that has just been devalued
items.why: Clearing currency = moeda de liquidação: aquela em que se liquidam os pagamentos internacionais.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Geopolitical shifts are beginning to ___ the trade routes we took for granted."
items.why: To reshape = remodelar: mudar a forma das rotas antes tidas como certas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em discussões estratégicas de negócios. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board must sign off on any change to our clearing currency." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We'll roll out the diversified routing plan corridor by corridor." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the ten-year scenario." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar.

items.q: "The team drafted contingency plans but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry them to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, com never, eles não o fizeram.

items.q: "Hedging one currency won't move the needle on our overall exposure." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível; com won't, não muda nada relevante.
